policy_title: Invest £3.4 Billion in NHS Technology and Productivity
stated: The Conservative Party will invest £3.4 billion in new technology to transform the NHS, making the NHS App the single front door for services, using AI to free up staff time, replacing outdated computers, digitising processes with the Federated Data Platform, and funding technology for faster scan analysis.

source.quote: We will invest £3.4 billion in new technology to transform the NHS for staff and for patients. The NHS Productivity Plan will see NHS productivity grow by 1.9% a year from 2025-26 – unlocking £35 billion of cumulative savings by the end of the decade.

bearing_set.reason: The entire policy is directed at NHS capacity and access — faster scan analysis, AI freeing staff time, and the NHS App as a service front door all directly affect waiting times, GP/diagnostic access, and delivered healthcare capacity.

The Federated Data Platform and NHS App as 'single front door' involve centralising/federating patient health records at scale — a concrete mechanism affecting the privacy indicator under O9, and one that has already attracted substantive public and regulatory debate (e.g. the Palantir FDP contract controversy).

The Federated Data Platform and making the NHS App a centralised 'single front door' aggregate patient health data at scale, raising a non-negligible privacy/surveillance concern against the privacy indicator.
£3.4bn of public spending must be sourced; if unfunded or borrowed rather than from efficiency savings, it materially affects the debt sustainability / funded-vs-borrowed indicator.

membership_note: The policy's primary effect is on healthcare access (O3); secondary bearings arise from patient data centralisation (O10/privacy) and the fiscal cost (O12). Prosperity (O13) and workforce quality (O4) effects are too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar given the policy's NHS-internal scope.
